newsitem.title: USA: TCI says customer falloff easing.
newsitem.headline: TCI says customer falloff easing.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said on Thursday a 70,000 net drop in U.S. cable-TV customers last summer was over and the company had won back some of the losses in September, October and November.

Brendan Clouston, chief executive of the company's TCI Communications cable business with 14 million subscribers, said only 10-15 percent of the net customer loss could be attributed to rival satellite-television technologies.
TCI and other cable operators' shares have been off sharply this year because Wall Street fears that satellite television and other technologies will end the cable industry's long history of growth.
TCI and other cable operators last spring sharply raised rates, a more likely cause for the customer drop, Clouston said in a telephone conference call with journalists.
TCI had 70,000 fewer cable customers on September 30 than June 30 but had posted net gains of 10,000-15,000 in September and October. Net gains were continuing in November, he said.
Another executive said TCI had per-cable-customer revenues in the third quarter of $38.10, up from about $36 in the second quarter.
